title: Digital Transformation: It's More Than Just New Technology

textData.text: At our latest Lunch & Learn, presented by Ruby Lutwama, we explored how digital transformation is about more than technology—it's about continuously finding better ways to work.
It All Starts with One Simple Question
That question often leads to others:
Technology is simply the tool that helps answer those questions.
The Four Stages of Digital Transformation
Think of digital transformation as a journey rather than a single destination. Most organisations move through four key stages, with each one building on the last.
Every journey starts somewhere, and for most businesses, it starts with digitisation.
Instead of filling in paper forms, filing documents in cabinets, or manually completing records, businesses move these processes online.
While this may seem like a small change, it creates immediate benefits:
Less risk of losing important documents
Once information is digital, the next question naturally follows.
"Why should a person do this if a system can do it automatically?"
Automation removes repetitive, manual tasks that consume valuable time every day.
Instead of spending hours on routine administration, employees can focus on work that actually requires human thinking, creativity, and problem-solving.
Knowing what to do with it is where the real value lies.
"What's happening right now... and what's likely to happen next?"
That's a significant shift, because decisions become proactive instead of reactive.
Of course, we can't talk about digital transformation without mentioning AI.
AI is everywhere right now—and for good reason.
It can help with tasks such as:
AI isn't here to replace everyone.
It's here to remove repetitive tasks so people can spend more time solving problems, being creative, and making informed decisions.
The organisations that benefit most from AI are the ones that see it as a partner—not a replacement.
Digital Transformation Isn't One Big Project
One of the biggest misconceptions about digital transformation is that it happens after installing one new system.
In reality, it's a continuous process of making improvements over time.
A typical journey might look something like this:
Add AI where it creates value.
Individually, these improvements may seem small.
Together, they create a connected digital ecosystem that helps businesses work smarter every day.
Digital transformation is less of a destination and more of an ongoing journey.
So, How Do You Know If It Worked?
Launching a new system is exciting, but success isn't measured on go-live day.
It's measured months later by the impact it has on the business.
✅ Can we see what's happening in real time?
, then your digital transformation is delivering real business value.
What Does the Future Look Like?
Businesses are moving away from reacting to problems and towards predicting them before they happen.
That's where digital transformation is heading—and we're only getting started.
New software will appear every year.
The organisations that succeed won't necessarily be the ones with the newest technology.
They'll be the ones willing to keep learning, adapting, and improving.
Because digital transformation has never really been about technology.
It's always been about people finding better ways to work.
The future belongs to businesses that stay curious, embrace change, and never stop improving.

title: The Riddle Board: Where Every Week Brings a New Mystery

textData.text: To celebrate this ongoing tradition, we asked everyone to share some of their favourite riddles from the board. 🔍
A man is driving his car when it suddenly breaks down in front of a hotel.
He goes inside, is instantly bankrupt, and loses everything.
If you throw me out the window, you'll leave a grieving wife, but drop me in the middle of a door, and you might just save a life.
What goes up a chimney down, but does not go down a chimney up?
I come once a minute, twice in a moment, but never in a thousand years.
Thirty white horses on a red hill,
Think you've figured them out? Here's the story behind the Riddle Board while you decide on your answers.
What started as a single riddle on a whiteboard in August 2025 quickly became one of our office's favourite traditions.

It all began when Gustav posted the very first riddle. The rules were simple: whoever guessed the correct answer earned the right to put up the next riddle. What followed was months of friendly competition, creative thinking, and plenty of moments where everyone was convinced they had the answer—only to discover they were completely off track!

As the riddles kept coming, so did the competition. A scoreboard was introduced, and every correct answer earned valuable points and bragging rights 🏆. The whiteboard became more than just a place for notes and reminders; it became a daily destination where colleagues would stop by to test their problem-solving skills.

When we moved offices in January 2026, the tradition moved with us 📦. With two new team members joining the challenge, the scoreboard was reset, and everyone started with a clean slate. It was a fresh opportunity for both seasoned riddle-solvers and newcomers to compete for the top spot.

The riddles came in all shapes and sizes. Some were related to the work we do, challenging us to think about familiar concepts in new ways. Others required us to think completely outside the box 💡, often leading to lively discussions and creative theories. There were even a few mathematical brainteasers that had everyone reaching for calculators, notebooks, and occasionally a second opinion!

One of the best parts of the Riddle Board has been the way it brings people together. Whether someone solves a riddle in minutes or spends days trying to figure it out, the conversations, laughter, and collaboration that happen along the way have become just as important as finding the correct answer.
The competition continues, the scoreboard keeps growing 📈, and one thing is certain: there is always another riddle waiting on the whiteboard. 😄

"Ever tried flying a kite with one corner missing? No matter how strong the wind is, it just won’t lift. It flutters, spins, and eventually nose-dives. Leadership works the same way."
The VISA Model, created by Christo Nel, is one of those frameworks that makes you go,
and together they form what’s called the
Each side of the kite represents a different style of leadership, and just like in real life, when one side is pulling too hard or another is neglected, things start wobbling. Balance is everything.
Visionary leaders are the “what if” people. They see things before others do - ideas, trends, and possibilities that don’t exist yet.
They’re the ones sketching the future on napkins, starting sentences with

and inspiring the rest of us to believe. But sometimes, they forget that not everyone lives in their heads. They can move so fast into tomorrow that the rest of the team is still trying to find their shoes today.
Pair your big ideas with someone who loves the details. They’ll help your dream find its wings.

These are the glue people - the ones who make work feel human. They remember birthdays, notice when someone’s off their game, and somehow turn meetings into meaningful conversations. They believe success is a
The challenge? Sometimes they care so much about harmony that tough calls get delayed or softened.
Leading with heart doesn’t mean avoiding hard things. The best teams know how to disagree and stay connected.

Where others see chaos, they see patterns. They love turning ideas into processes, and chaos into checklists. They keep everyone organized, informed, and on schedule. They’re the people who actually make sure the plane
But if things get too structured, creativity can suffocate. Too many rules, and suddenly the team is stuck in process instead of progress.
Systems are amazing — just remember they exist to serve people, not the other way around.

These are the doers. The fixers. The “let’s just make it happen” people. When everyone else is still talking about it, they’ve already sent the email, booked the meeting, and ticked it off the list. They’re driven, decisive, and unstoppable — until they burn out.
Pause long enough to make sure you’re climbing the
mountain, not just the nearest one.
🧩 The Magic Is in the Mix
Each of these leadership styles is valuable on its own, but together, they’re unstoppable.
The point isn’t to be perfect at all four - it’s to know where your natural lift comes from, and where you might need a little tailwind from
Leadership isn’t about titles or job descriptions. It’s about influence - the way you show up for people, ideas, and challenges.
So here’s a quick reflection for you:
Once you know your shape, you can start building balance — in yourself and in your team. Because when all sides pull together, that’s when leadership really takes flight.

title: Lunch & Learn Recap: SAP Manufacturing Showdown: Process vs. Discrete

textData.text: Presented by: Jason Craig and Karla Uys
If you’ve ever wondered why making a bottle of soda is nothing like building a car, welcome to the world of

Let’s dive into how these two manufacturing types stack up, where they shine, and how SAP supports each like a champ.
🏭 Discrete Manufacturing: Think Pieces, Parts & Precision
This is your go-to method when you’re building stuff you can count, literally.
One unit at a time, clear-cut processes
Not a lot of “in-between” products, parts go from A to B to finished item
Based on individual orders (build 100 computers, not 100 liters)
It’s like building LEGO sets, every part has a place, and every set ends up the same (mostly).
🧪 Process Manufacturing: Welcome to the World of Batches, Blends & Beakers
This type is all about recipes and formulas. You're not assembling parts, you're transforming materials.
Liquid, flowy, sometimes smelly, but very precise
Bulk materials and intermediate storage are the norm
Batch or continuous process; recipes rule everything
It’s like baking a cake in a lab, exact measurements, strict rules, and a clean-up required between every batch.

title: Lunch & Learn Recap: Getting Comfortable with Git

textData.text: Whether you're a developer, business analyst, consultant, or technical writer — understanding Git can seriously level up how you collaborate and manage projects.
In our latest Lunch & Learn, we broke down the essentials of Git: what it is, why it matters, and how anyone (yes, anyone!) can start using it.
Git is a free, open-source version control system created by Linus Torvalds in 2005. Think of it as a
— it tracks every change, shows who made what edits, and makes it easy for teams to work on the same project without overwriting each other’s work.
Why Learn Git? Benefits for Developers and Beyond
Git was primarily built for developers to manage code, but its benefits stretch beyond programming. Here’s how Git supports different roles across your team:
Track every change in your codebase and collaborate without overwriting work
Use branches to develop features or fix bugs safely before merging
Suggest, review, and approve changes through pull requests for better quality control
See who changed what and when, making debugging and audits easier
Track edits in project plans, specs, or reports with a clear history and ability to revert mistakes
Stay aligned when multiple people update files or content simultaneously, avoiding confusion or version conflicts
Compare versions side-by-side, so editors, analysts, and managers can see exactly what was updated
Try new ideas or drafts in branches without disrupting the main work, then merge once finalized
Git’s version control and collaboration features help everyone—from engineers to project managers—work more transparently and efficiently.
The folder that holds your project and its change history
A snapshot of your project at a specific moment
A workspace to make changes without disrupting the main project
Combining changes from one branch into another
A shared version of your project (e.g., on GitHub or GitLab)
Here’s how a typical Git process flows:
– Copy the project to your machine.
– Create a workspace for your changes.
– Save your updates with a short message.
– Upload changes to the remote repo.
– Combine your updates into the main version.
This structure keeps teamwork smooth and structured — even across time zones.
How We Use Git at Work
At Lark & Stern, Git is at the heart of how our developers collaborate and stay organized. It helps us:
Keep our workflows clean and efficient.
No more “who changed this?” — Git always has the answer.
Where you begin depends on your style:
For hands-on folks (start with git clone, git commit, git push).
GitHub Desktop, Sourcetree, etc., for a more visual experience.
Tools like VS Code or IntelliJ come with Git baked in.
Pick your path — they all get you there.
✅ It improves how teams collaborate, organize, and version their work
✅ Even basic Git skills can make you a more effective team member
